clue.text: Full of energy, like many CID members

indicators.note: the members, or constituent parts, of the phrase many CID are taken apart and rebuilt into a new word

explanation.surface: A remark that detectives of the Criminal Investigation Department are mostly energetic types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' asks for the letters of MANY and CID to be rearranged: MANYCID becomes the answer. CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, the plain-clothes detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dynamic is vigorous and forceful, bursting with drive.

clue.text: Hoax about a sporting award? Player told to start again

indicators.note: about means around, the hoax word wrapped around the award

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or hoax them
a cap is awarded for playing for one's country

explanation.surface: A question about some prank involving a sports honour.
explanation.walkthrough: A CAP is awarded to a player picked for a national team. 'Player' here is a musician, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Da capo is the musical instruction telling a performer to go back to the beginning.

clue.text: Lack of ceremonial music for a Greek governor

parts.note: no means none, a lack of something
a march is music for parades and ceremonies

explanation.surface: A Greek official is said to be without a band at his ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomarch is the governor of a nome or nomos, a province of Greece.

clue.text: Discoursed about Aesop's lesson on the side perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue the lesson sits on top of the next piece

parts.note: each of Aesop's fables ends with a moral

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of side may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone talked about a fable's lesson as an aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SIDE into ISED, which goes under MORAL, as 'on' says in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To moralise is to lecture or pontificate about right and wrong.

clue.text: Takes in, like the local school?

explanation.surface: Someone grasps things, just like the neighbourhood school does.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a British comprehensive school, a state school for all abilities, is nicknamed a 'comp', so it 'comp-rehends'.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in an idea is to understand it; a British comprehensive school is jokingly said to include all.

clue.text: Dichromatic bird without feathers

parts.note: pie is an old name for the magpie
a bird with no feathers is bald, like a bald head

explanation.surface: A description of some two-toned bird that has lost all its plumage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dichromatic' looks like it describes the bird, but it is the definition; a piebald horse is patched black and white.
explanation.definitionFit: Piebald describes an animal patched in two colours, usually black and white.

clue.text: Joke made before injection in India

definitions.text: Joke made before injection in India

parts.words: Joke made before injection in India
parts.note: a play on words placed before a jab, slang for an injection, gives an Indian state

explanation.surface: Someone cracks a joke before giving an injection in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Put this joke before JAB, an injection, and you get PUNJAB, a state in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A play on words is a joke that turns on two senses of a word.

clue.text: Part of score associated with the film

explanation.surface: Something both a scorer's tally and a film credit share.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs not credited to a batsman, such as wides and byes.
explanation.definitionFit: A run not scored off the bat in cricket; also a film actor with a non-speaking crowd role.

clue.text: Singer in Mozart is terrible…

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words Mozart is terrible

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that a vocalist in an opera by Mozart is awful.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: dreary notes so long delayed

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
something long delayed is late

explanation.surface: The singer's notes are drab and come very late.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 7 down, so 'dreary notes' seems to describe the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A desolate place is bleak and cheerless.

clue.text: TV employee arrived with male artist

parts.note: to have arrived is to have come
RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist
a man is a male person

explanation.surface: A television worker turned up accompanied by a male painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the order arrived, artist, male: the clue lists male before artist, so the charade is rearranged into answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: A television studio employs operators who work the cameras.

clue.text: Tell-tale American emperor?

parts.note: from the playground taunt 'tell-tale tit', a tit being a sneak
US is short for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: A question whether some gossiping American could be an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell-tale tit' is a British children's taunt for a sneak. Titus was a Roman emperor of the first century AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a Roman ruler, son of Vespasian, who reigned AD 79 to 81.

clue.text: Fairy leading many to danger

indicators.note: the fairy comes first, at the head of the next piece, so it is placed in front

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian legend
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: A sprite luring a crowd of people into harm.
explanation.walkthrough: L as 'many' is a convention: the Roman numeral fifty stands for a large number.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious risk or jeopardy.

clue.text: For practice, dress before the last one

definitions.text: For practice, dress before the last one

parts.words: For practice, dress before the last one
parts.note: a practice run of a play; the dress version is the final run-through, held just before the real opening

explanation.surface: Advice to put on clothes for training before the final session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like a verb about clothes, but it is the 'dress' run-through of a play, the last practice before the opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre company's practice run of its show, the dress version being the final one with costumes.

clue.text: Instruments' one combination of notes from this?

definitions.text: Instruments' one combination of notes from this?

parts.note: harps are stringed instruments
I is the Roman numeral one
a chord is notes played together

explanation.surface: A question whether one combination of notes comes from these instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a chord can be played on this keyboard instrument, whose strings are plucked like a harp's.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument whose strings are plucked, able to play chords.

clue.text: Unusually posh shop centre shining in the dark

indicators.note: done unusually, the letters of posh shop centre are put in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A remark about a glowing, upmarket shopping mall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' tells you to rearrange POSHSHOPCENTRE, all fourteen letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosphorescent things give off a glow without heat, visible at night.

clue.text: Chios'-- last resort for an old grammarian

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it asks for the letters of Chios and last to be sorted again

explanation.surface: A Greek island is the final holiday spot for an elderly scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place, but read as 're-sort' it rearranges CHIOSLAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholiast was an ancient commentator who wrote explanatory notes on classical texts.

clue.text: Jack's in the drink

parts.note: jack is a sailor, AB for able seaman, followed by S

explanation.surface: A sailor has fallen into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the drink' is slang for fallen into water, but the drink here is the green spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green wormwood spirit.

clue.text: Where one learns to recognize a shoal of fish after embarkation?

indicators.note: the shoal comes after the embarkation, so it is placed second

parts.note: boarding a ship or plane is embarking
a school is a shoal of fish

explanation.surface: A question about where you learn to spot a shoal after getting aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A residential school where pupils live during term; 'after' puts the fish group behind the boarding.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential school is a place of education where pupils live and study.

clue.text: Sort of quaint eastern relic

indicators.note: sort here means arrange, so the letters of quaint are reordered

explanation.surface: Some charming old object from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique is an old collectable object surviving from the past.

clue.text: About what's owed -— it's late!

parts.note: over means about, as in a fuss over something
a debt is what is due

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that a payment owed has not been made on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has passed its expected time.

clue.text: According to Housman, the loveliest of trees

definitions.text: According to Housman, the loveliest of trees

parts.words: According to Housman, the loveliest of trees
parts.note: A. E. Housman's poem in A Shropshire Lad opens by naming a blossoming tree as loveliest

explanation.surface: A quotation of a poet's favourite tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem opens 'Loveliest of trees, the cherry now / Is hung with bloom along the bough'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet A. E. Housman named this blossoming fruit tree loveliest of all.

clue.text: Such value is of the essence!

definitions.text: Such value is of the essence!

parts.words: Such value is of the essence!
parts.note: the kind of worth that lies in a thing's own nature, its very essence, rather than in anything outside it

explanation.surface: An exclamation that some quality is fundamental.
explanation.definitionFit: Inherent worth belongs to a thing's essential nature, as opposed to extrinsic value.

clue.text: One French boy or girl

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
René is a French boy's name

explanation.surface: Asking whether a French child is a boy or a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a girl's name, from the Greek goddess of peace.

clue.text: A hanger-on, the caricaturist, …

explanation.surface: A clinging parasite, and also a famous cartoonist.
explanation.walkthrough: John Leech was a Victorian caricaturist for the British magazine Punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloodsucking worm is the image of a parasite who clings to others; John Leech drew cartoons for Punch.

clue.text: … to what French headgear?

parts.note: que is French for what

explanation.surface: A continuation of the previous clue, asking what a Frenchman wears on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link it to 23 across as one sentence. A toque is a chef's tall white hat, or a small brimless hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A toque is a tall white chef's hat or a brimless woman's hat.

clue.text: Pantomime mother, some say, also a duck

indicators.note: some say tells us these words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: Mother Goose is a traditional British Christmas pantomime
and means also
the word a, spoken unstressed as 'uh', is the sound written ER at the end of the bird's name

explanation.surface: A remark about a panto character and a waterbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' asks for 'Goose and a' to be heard: spoken in a non-rhotic accent it sounds like the bird's name. Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show, and Mother Goose is one of its stock stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The goosander is a fish-eating sawbill bird of the merganser family.

clue.text: Georgia's word for petrol

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone from the American state of Georgia naming fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: In America petrol is called gas, which suits a word from Georgia, the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is the American term for motor fuel.

clue.text: Unseeing like Samson in Gaza

explanation.surface: A comparison of a blind person to the Bible's Samson.
explanation.walkthrough: In Judges, Samson is blinded by the Philistines in Gaza; Milton's phrase 'Eyeless in Gaza' gave Aldous Huxley a novel title.
explanation.definitionFit: Blind, as Milton described Samson in Samson Agonistes: 'Eyeless in Gaza, at the mill with slaves'.

clue.text: Too irresolute to try and hide perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of try and hide might be put another way

explanation.surface: Someone too indecisive either to attempt something or to conceal themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TRYHIDE into the answer; 'Too' and 'to' are link words framing the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithery describes someone dithering, indecisive and nervously hesitant.
